preamble: Debuccalization of coda [d] to a glottal stop [ʔ]. The clearest case is Lhasa (Standard) Tibetan, where the Classical Tibetan final -d was lost as an oral stop and replaced by a phonemic glottal stop, usually with umlaut fronting of the preceding vowel, as in Bod 'Tibet' > [pʰø̀ʔ]. Unlike the widespread glottal replacement of voiceless /t/, glottal replacement of voiced /d/ is rarely documented.

examples.note: Final -d is replaced by a glottal stop; the preceding vowel is fronted by umlaut.

examples.from: Classical Tibetan པད pad 'lotus' (from Sanskrit padma)
examples.note: Final -d surfaces as a glottal stop, also in the compound ཞབས་པད zhabs pad [ɕʌpɛʔ].
